title: Earth's seasons
text: Earth's seasons are caused primarily by its roughly 23.5-degree axial tilt. A hemisphere tilted toward the Sun receives more direct sunlight and longer days, while the opposite hemisphere receives less direct sunlight and shorter days. The hemispheres therefore have opposite seasons at the same time. Changing Earth-Sun distance is not the main cause; Earth is closest to the Sun in early January, during Northern Hemisphere winter.

title: Drinking-water treatment
text: Water safety depends on source quality, treatment, storage, and testing. Boiling can inactivate many pathogens but does not remove dissolved metals, salts, or many chemical contaminants. Filtration performance depends on pore size and filter media, so a claim should identify the contaminant and treatment mechanism.

title: Solar electricity and storage
text: Solar photovoltaic panels convert light into electricity. Battery storage can shift energy from sunny periods to evening demand. Comparing a system requires more than one metric: conversion efficiency, storage duration, round-trip losses, cost, maintenance, and local grid constraints all matter.

title: Comparing conflicting evidence
text: When sources conflict, compare publication date, methodology, sample size, uncertainty, incentives, and whether the claim is an observation or an interpretation. A careful synthesis preserves disagreement, cites each claim, and explains why one source may apply better to the question.

title: Formula One overview
text: Formula One is an international single-seater motor-racing championship. A season is organized around Grands Prix, with teams designing cars to a technical rule set and drivers competing for points. A useful explanation should distinguish the sporting regulations, technical regulations, qualifying, race strategy, tyres, and the championship points system.

title: How a car moves
text: A road car moves when its powertrain produces torque and the drivetrain applies force at the tyres. Acceleration also depends on traction, mass, gearing, aerodynamic drag, rolling resistance, and road slope. Fuel and battery vehicles differ in how energy is stored and converted, but both are limited by available power, grip, and losses.

title: Battery storage basics
text: A battery stores energy through reversible electrochemical reactions. Capacity describes how much charge can be stored, while power describes how quickly energy can be delivered. Cycle life, temperature, depth of discharge, charging rate, safety controls, and efficiency affect practical service life.

title: Weather and climate
text: Weather describes atmospheric conditions over short periods and local areas. Climate describes statistical patterns over longer periods. A single cold day does not by itself disprove long-term warming, while a long-term trend cannot predict the exact weather on a particular day.

title: What a computer program does
text: A computer program is a sequence of instructions interpreted or compiled for a processor. Data moves through memory and storage, while the operating system manages processes, files, permissions, and devices. Performance depends on workload, algorithms, memory access, parallelism, and hardware limits rather than processor speed alone.

title: Internet and local networks
text: A network moves data between devices using agreed protocols. Local networks connect nearby devices, while the Internet links many independent networks. Offline software can still use local files and computation, but it cannot retrieve current remote information without a network path.

title: Reasoning about health information
text: Health claims should distinguish symptoms, diagnoses, treatments, risks, and evidence quality. A mechanism that sounds plausible is not proof that an intervention works. Urgent symptoms, severe reactions, breathing difficulty, chest pain, or possible poisoning require professional or emergency help rather than an offline information tool.

title: Using historical evidence
text: Historical explanations combine primary evidence, later scholarship, chronology, context, and competing interpretations. A document created during an event can provide direct evidence but may reflect its author's position. A later account can add synthesis but may depend on incomplete or selective records.
